market_story: MISO's coal fleet is predominantly self-committed by regulated utilities (2023/24 SOM: must-run status on 56%/53% of regulated coal starts; offers at cost, system price-cost markup +3.0%/-2.5%). A self-committed unit's boiler never goes cold -- its min-load block rides through the night -- so ramping its committed band up in the morning costs fuel, not a $100/MW cold start. The model was amortizing that start into the committed band's energy offer anyway (P1 startup amortization over raw P0 run lengths), pricing 15 GW of coal $8-15/MWh above its measured delivered-fuel SRMC and handing its mid-merit energy to gas CC/CT -- the inverted merit order behind the CEMS-basis coal under-run (-34/-42 TWh 2023/24) and the low CO2. miso-59 turns on the existing warm-boiler exemption (coal_warm_committed): committed coal re-enters merit at cost, exactly as the IMM measures MISO conduct.
